principles.statement: Measure capability, not completion.
Record understood, recalled, transferred and retained as separate task/time evidence categories without claiming they are independent latent abilities.
Attempt before reveal when the task is intended to practice or measure retrieval.
Use spaced review without interpreting scheduler state as mastery.
Treat captions and L1 translation as scaffolds whose visibility should match the learning objective.
Do not use one irreversible known/mastered boolean as the sole lexical learner state; derive graded state from attempt evidence.
Match the learner-state claim to the task: recognition cannot unlock recall/production status, and scaffolded recall cannot be labeled independent production.
Require delayed re-demonstration before labeling lexical evidence retained.
Treat useful chunks as lexical targets and record phrase-level cue/support information when measuring them.
Near A0, prioritize useful spoken/written form-meaning connections first and deepen use/collocation knowledge progressively instead of requiring total lexical mastery up front.
Near A0, allow strategic Vietnamese support; do not enforce an English-only policy as a product virtue.
Use Vietnamese to reduce unnecessary access cost while keeping the English form/audio/context as the object of learning.
Hide answer-bearing Vietnamese during independent comprehension/recall probes and record any revealed support before interpreting success.
Prefer progressive disclosure of the smallest useful scaffold over permanently visible full translation.
Fade Vietnamese based on demonstrated lower-support performance, not an arbitrary day or vocabulary-count rule; calibrate the exact threshold experimentally.
Keep task instructions, lexical glosses, context hints, contrastive notes, feedback and full translation as distinct scaffold types in data and UX.
Judge a scaffold by later unsupported English performance and task access, not by immediate accuracy or ease alone.
Separate speech perception/decoding evidence from message-comprehension evidence in listening tasks.
Capture an audio-only attempt before revealing answer-bearing transcript/captions when measuring independent listening.
When short-message comprehension fails, diagnose the critical decoding/form-meaning step instead of only replaying or revealing the answer.
Record speaker, replay count, transcript visibility and other listening support provenance with every scored attempt.
Do not use strict full dictation as the sole beginner decoding measure; minimize or explicitly label orthographic production demands.
Teach and test known lexical targets in connected speech and later vary speakers/phonetic contexts rather than training one isolated recording only.
Integrate bottom-up listening work with message-level comprehension and metacognitive feedback; neither phonetic drills nor strategies alone define the curriculum.
Use unseen parallel utterances and, when feasible, new speakers to test listening transfer rather than memorization of the trained recording.
Use retrieval as a learning event only after the learner has enough initial access to make a meaningful attempt; do not confuse repeated failure with desirable difficulty.
Optimize review for delayed unsupported performance per minute, not for repetition count, card count or immediate accuracy.
Prefer adaptive spacing informed by learner/item history over a universal 1-3-7-style ritual, while keeping a simple fallback when data are sparse.
Do not treat expanding versus equal spacing as a product doctrine; the absolute amount of spacing and retention horizon matter more than one universal relative-spacing pattern.
Select review tasks to match the capability evidence needed: recognition, recall, aural access and changed-context use are not interchangeable simply because they share one due date.
For retrieval tasks, capture the attempt before answer-bearing feedback; then correct efficiently rather than enforcing a universal feedback delay.
Keep scheduler memory state, due state and language-capability evidence as separate data models; a due interval or predicted recall probability never sets mastery.
Derive scheduler outcomes from observable task evidence and support provenance instead of requiring learners to self-grade memory; any mapping to FSRS grades is a product calibration choice.
Treat desired retention and review workload as an explicit product tradeoff to calibrate against learning gain, backlog and return behavior.
Never label an exact trained-context replay or retest as transfer; record it as retention/trained-context evidence.
For near-A0 transfer, start with unseen parallel items that change one bounded dimension while preserving the target communicative relation.
Increase contextual novelty from demonstrated capability rather than maximizing variation by default.
Keep non-target vocabulary, grammar and interface demands inside a controlled novelty budget when interpreting a changed-context failure.
Record transfer evidence by elicitation type such as comprehension, recognition, controlled production and open production; do not let one task certify all of them.
Require a productive changed-context attempt before claiming independent productive transfer; receptive transfer remains valuable but narrower evidence.
Near A0, prefer constrained production when it isolates the target; free conversation is not required to test every lexical item or construction.
Track exactly which context, speaker, modality, cue and response dimensions changed for every scored transfer probe.
Treat a transfer probe as both measurement and learning exposure; preserve first-seen provenance and never reuse it as fresh unseen evidence.
Sample transfer according to evidence need and learner-time budget; calibrate novelty level and probe frequency against later unseen performance.
